generatedProse.concept-context: The School of Sport uses several exam types, and each asks for something different. A multiple-choice exam might test your recall of training principles or anatomy. An essay exam asks you to argue a case about coaching practice or a sport policy, weighing the evidence. A short answer exam wants precise definitions of key concepts. Knowing which type you face tells you what good revision looks like.
generatedProse.worked-example:
Two sport coaching students are told their module has an essay exam on coaching methods, and both begin preparing.

Tom revises as he would for any test: memorising definitions, coaching models and study names, ready to write them down. He knows a great deal of detail, but he has not practised building an argument, which is what a coaching essay exam asks for.

Amara first asks what this type of exam is testing. An essay exam wants a reasoned argument, so she practises planning answers, weighing competing approaches to a training session, and writing to time. She memorises fewer isolated facts, but she can use the evidence to make a case.

Both revised hard. Only Amara matched her preparation to what an essay exam demands.
generatedProse.summary: School of Sport exams come in several forms: multiple-choice exams test recall, essay exams want a reasoned argument, short answer exams reward precise explanation, and others test applying methods or reading data. You can now identify the main types and see why the type you face should shape your revision. The next lesson turns to why a revision strategy matters.

check.body: In the worked example, why was Amara's preparation better suited to an essay exam?

items.text: She practised building and writing a reasoned argument, weighing approaches, which is what an essay exam asks for.
She memorised more definitions and coaching models than Tom.
She revised for more hours than Tom.
She started revising the night before the exam.

feedback.correct: That's right. Practising a reasoned argument matched what a coaching essay exam demands.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Look for the preparation that fits what an essay exam is actually asking for.
feedback.incorrectFinal: An essay exam asks for a reasoned argument, and Amara practised exactly that. Memorising more, or longer hours, does not match the task.
